newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's ruling party seeks bigger share of vote.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's ruling party seeks bigger share of vote.

text.p: Indonesia's ruling Golkar party is hoping to improve its share of the vote in next year's general elections, the Jakarta Post reported on Thursday.

"We have to increase our victory from what we gained in 1992. If Golkar got 68 percent then, we would consider our victory solid if we could increase our number of votes in 1997," party chairman Harmoko (Eds: one word), who is also minister for information, was quoted as saying.
Party officials, beginning a three-day annual congress on Wednesday, said they hoped to increase Golkar's share of the vote to 71 percent in 1997.
Golkar has said it will contest all 425 elective seats of the 500-member parliament in the elections scheduled for June next year. The other 75 seats are nominated by the military.

The other two political parties legally allowed to contest elections in Indonesia are the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
In 1987 elections, Golkar won 73 percent of the vote. But in 1992, that share dropped to 68 percent of votes cast and 282 seats, the PPP 17 percent and 62 seats, and the PDI 15 percent and 56 seats.
Only 400 seats were at stake in the previous elections, with the other 100 members being nominated.
